domain: EU carbon-market compliance - installation-level allowance shortfall prediction (EU institution publisher, EUTL public extracts)
prediction_question: For a stationary installation covered by the EU Emissions Trading System, will its verified emissions for compliance year t exceed the free allocation it holds for year t (a net-short year: the operator must buy allowances at auction/secondary market to surrender, or face the excess-emissions penalty), given its verified-emissions, free-allocation and surrender history through year t-1, its already-published year-t free allocation, its registry (country) and its name/identifier?
prediction_time: 30 April of compliance year t, the surrender deadline that closes year t-1's compliance cycle: by then the installation's verified emissions and surrendered allowances for year t-1 are published in the Union Registry (verified emissions are due by 31 March and surrendered allowances by 30 April), and year t's free allocation is known in advance (fixed by the phase-4 national implementation measures decisions recorded in the registry - the extract already carries ALLOCATION for years up to 2030). Year t's verified emissions are not yet observed anywhere: they are reported by 31 March t+1. The extract refreshes daily (SNAPSHOT_DATE column, last-modified 2026-10-20), so a monthly refresh of this task is honest.
target_definition: Binary, computed from the source row of (installation, year t): VERIFIED_EMISSIONS(t) > ALLOCATION(t), where ALLOCATION is the free allocation recorded in the registry for year t and VERIFIED_EMISSIONS is the independently verified emissions figure. Unit: both are tonnes CO2-equivalent per installation-year (1 allowance = 1 tonne); the comparison is unit-free within the source's own frame (no external threshold or datum is involved). Frame restriction: installation-years where both VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION are numeric ('n/a' rows - not-yet-operating, excluded or closed sites - are out of frame and their handling must be pinned at construction). Label source columns VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION at year t are recorded in label_source_columns and must be absent from the shipped features; feature rows may use emissions/allocation/surrender values only for years <= t-1 plus year-t allocation.

construction_script: candidates/eutl-installation-net-short/source/build.py (stdlib only; single bulk GET of the daily extract plus the EEA aggregate zip for the in-build cross-check; --panel-file/--eea-file accept local copies for a full-assertion coordinator dry run)
split_strategy: Temporal at installation-year grain, one row per (installation, compliance year t): train t <= 2019 (2005-2019), eval 2020-2022, holdout 2023-2025, all restricted to in-frame installation-years (both VERIFIED_EMISSIONS and ALLOCATION numeric). Measured on the 2026-10-20 snapshot (measured_net_short_by_year in notes.md): every year 2005-2025 carries both classes; eligible rows per year range 7,402 (2025) to 11,520 (2012); the net-short base rate drifts by phase - 27.7-31.3% in phase 1/2 (2005-2012), 56.4-71.5% in phase 3 (2013-2020), 69.8-80.6% in phase 4 (2021-2025) - a documented phenomenon property (free-allocation share fell and benchmarks tightened while the cap declined), the analogue of the flunet COVID-era base-rate break; construction must document it, not smooth it. Entities recur across windows by construction (23,708 installation keys observed over 2005-2030 rows), so the row id must be the composite (registry, installation, year) and the recurring-entity property declared, not mistaken for split leakage; positives cluster weakly at the installation level (an installation's net-short status is autocorrelated year to year), so the clustered count to report is distinct installations going net-short in a window, measured at construction.

novelty_check.theirs: The publisher (European Commission DG CLIMA) publishes the raw installation-year panel (verified emissions, free allocation, surrendered units) as daily bulk extracts, and the EEA publishes country-sector-year aggregates plus a data viewer. Carbon-market research literature models firm-level abatement and allowance prices, but ships no task: no splits, no labels, no scored contract.
novelty_check.ours: A binary installation-year net-short task on the Union Registry public extracts (will verified emissions exceed free allocation for the coming compliance year), with disjoint temporal splits across 2005-2025, prediction timing pinned at the 30 April surrender deadline, recurring-entity property declared, and a scored contract for coding-agent evaluation. No ML-ready version of this formulation exists in public catalogs.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.

baseline.note: Measured on the bytes being released (fetched from staging 420810883, digest-verified, gate --accept before scoring), not a rebuild. Persistence is recorded beside every model number. No holdout AUC is quoted: the holdout never enters a workdir.
